newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance to borrow $1.0 bln abroad - paper.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance to borrow $1.0 bln abroad - paper.

text.p: India's Reliance group of companies plans to raise $1.0 billion through debt issues in global markets, a financial daily reported on Tuesday.
The Business Standard newspaper said the petrochemicals and oil refining major group will tap foreign markets to finance diversification into the telecommunications and power sectors.

The 110 billion rupee conglomerate was planning to tap the Samurai and Euro markets in 1997/98 (April-March) and 1998/99 to reduce its debt exposure in the US markets, the paper reported Matthew Panikar, managing director of Reliance Europe Ltd as saying.
The paper said group flagship Reliance Industries recently concluded a 100-year $100 million Yankee bond issue.
The group plans to raise total debt of $450 million in 1997/98 (April-March), the paper said.

About $250 million would be used to finance the Reliance Patalganaga power project, a 1,000 megawatt liquefied natural gas plant to be set up near the group's 15 million metric tonne per annum capacity refinery, Business Standard said.

Financial arrangements for the project are expected to be complete by the end of financial 1997/98 (March-April). Citibank, Hongkong and Shanghai Bank Corporation and CS First Boston hold the advisory mandate for the project, the paper said.

Business Standard said another $200 million will be sourced from foreign debt markets for Reliance's cellular telecommunications project. Financial arrangements for the project are expected to be complete by the end of the current financial year, it said.

The paper said Reliance is also planning to tap golbal debt markets to finance its $1.2 billion basic telecommunications project in the western Indian state of Gujarat. The issue was likely to be in 1998/99, it said.
